question: The number of on-field umpires in cricket matches is _______?
solution:
The correct answer is __**2.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Generally, there are **two on-field umpires** in cricket matches.
 
• One umpire typically **stands behind the stumps at the bowler's end**, which provides a clear view of the bowler's action, the line and length of the delivery, and the batsman's shots.
 
• The second umpire **stands at square leg or a little behind,** allowing them to judge line calls more accurately, such as wides or no-balls due to front foot faults. They can also observe short runs and can assist the main umpire with decisions that require a side-on perspective.
 
• The umpires have the power to make decisions according to the 'Laws of Cricket' regarding all aspects of play, such as fair and unfair play, player conduct, and decisions on whether batsmen are out or not.
 
• In addition to these two on-field umpires, there is also usually a **third (off-field) umpire **and **sometimes a fourth umpire**, who assist the on-field umpires with certain decisions using video replays and other technologies, among other duties.
